clue.text: Authenticity of early IT development

indicators.note: a thing in development is being reshaped, so the letters of EARLY IT are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone praises how genuine computing was in its pioneering days.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'early IT development' as a phrase from tech history, hiding that 'development' is an instruction to rework the letters of EARLY IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the authenticity of something is its being real rather than fake, which is its reality.

clue.text: Hard to single out particular nationality

indicators.note: 'out' in the sense of out of order: the letters are knocked out of their arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone finds it difficult to pick out one specific nationality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single out' looks like a phrasal verb meaning pick; split it, and 'out' is the anagram instruction acting on H plus SINGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the definition names a category, and the answer is one member of it, the nationality of people from England.

clue.text: Left furthest part of rocky projection

parts.note: the edge is the furthest part of something

explanation.surface: A climber is left clinging to the very tip of an outcrop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Furthest part of rocky projection' reads as one phrase; the definition is only the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A description rather than a synonym: a ledge is a narrow shelf of rock jutting out from a cliff face.

clue.text: Drama of Mad Hatter's final performance

indicators.note: a mad arrangement is a crazy one
the final part of 'performance' is its last letter

parts.note: anagram fodder; the 's joins it to the next word

explanation.surface: A review of the Mad Hatter's last turn on stage, straight out of Alice in Wonderland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mad Hatter is a single character from Alice in Wonderland, so 'Mad' passes as part of his name rather than an instruction to scramble HATTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the art form: a career in drama is a career in the theatre.

clue.text: Agree adjustment to student year with alacrity

indicators.note: an adjustment rearranges things, here the letters of AGREE

parts.note: L = learner, as on a learner driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: Someone agrees, quickly and willingly, to a change in a student's year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adjustment to' looks like it is adjusting the student year; it acts only on AGREE, and L and Y are then tacked on.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverbial phrase for an adverb: alacrity is keen readiness, so acting with it is acting eagerly.

clue.text: Shenanigans opposed by civil service

parts.note: CS, the initials of the Civil Service, Britain's body of government officials

explanation.surface: Some mischief meets resistance from the government's officials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' just joins the pieces: ANTI then CS.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words mean silly or mischievous carryings-on.

clue.text: Over a mile to get home, having dined with dispatch

indicators.note: turning something over flips it, so MILE is read backwards

explanation.surface: A walker goes more than a mile to get back home after a quick dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over a mile' passes for 'more than a mile'; here 'over' turns MILE backwards. 'Dispatch' means kill here, not speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A euphemism shared by both words: to dispatch an enemy is to kill them off, the sense the surface's speedy dinner hides.

clue.text: List set to reform the most unproductive

indicators.note: to reform something is to form it again differently, so SET is rearranged

explanation.surface: A manager draws up a list meant to shake up the least productive staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'List' is a noun in the surface but a verb in the wordplay: to list is to lean, as a ship does.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of lean in its sense of meagre: lean years are ones with poor harvests.

clue.text: Judge equipment with time to sort out storage facilities

indicators.note: 'sort out' as in rearrange: SORT's letters are put in a new order

parts.note: a ref, or referee, judges play
a rig is a set of equipment
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone is told to judge the kit and take time to organise the storerooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort out' reads as tidy up the storage; 'out' is the instruction and SORT the letters it acts on.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by function: fridges are cabinets whose job is keeping food stored cold.

clue.text: Advanced alternative, say, in modern times

indicators.note: an alternative version of EG is its letters in another order
being in something means sitting inside it

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the modern era of dates
say = e.g., for example; its alternative order is GE

explanation.surface: A progressive option is described as belonging to the present day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advanced' looks like it means progressive, matching 'modern times'; it means advanced in years.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortened idiom: 'advanced' stands for advanced in years, which describes someone old.

clue.text: Requiring power to let a cleric off

indicators.note: off as in gone wrong, like milk that is off: the letters are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: A demand that a clergyman be let off the hook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let a cleric off' reads as excusing a priest; 'off' is the scramble instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: an electrical appliance is one that runs on mains power.

clue.text: Point of scandal engulfing the City

indicators.note: to engulf is to swallow up completely

parts.note: dirt = scandal, as in digging up dirt
EC is the postcode of the City of London, the financial district

explanation.surface: The heart of a scandal that swamps London's financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' is a verb: to point someone somewhere is to direct them.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb for verb: you point a visitor the right way by directing them.

clue.text: Get right part for radio

explanation.surface: Someone is told to find the correct component for a radio set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get right' looks like 'get correct'; the two words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by function: the receiver is the component that picks up the broadcast signal.

clue.text: Cast doubt on church claim about one point

indicators.note: 'about' in its sense of around

parts.note: N, north, is one point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone disputes what the church asserts on a single matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One point' reads as one item of argument; it is a compass point, N.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb for a verb: you question a claim, or challenge it, when you doubt it.

clue.text: Radio audience play silent Cupid when love is absent

indicators.note: something absent is missing, so the love, O, is taken out of EROS
letters at play move about freely, so SILENT's letters shift into a new order

parts.note: Cupid is the Roman name for Eros; EROS without love (O, zero in tennis) is ERS

explanation.surface: A radio drama has an actor in the non-speaking role of Cupid, oddly with no romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play silent Cupid' reads as a non-speaking part; 'play' is the scramble instruction. Love is O because a zero score in tennis is love.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the people who tune in to a radio programme are its listeners.

clue.text: Mixture of ancient English

parts.note: ancient things belong to the past

explanation.surface: A blend of Old English, the language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ancient English' suggests Old English; the words split into PAST and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A general word for a specific one: paste is a soft blend, of flour and water for example.

clue.text: Waterlogged land damages hotel

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or damage
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Flooded ground is wrecking a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a plausible news line about flooding; the verb 'damages' supplies MARS.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a marsh is low ground that stays soaked with water.

clue.text: Unprofessional of a graduate with true potential

indicators.note: TRUE is only the potential for a word: its letters could still become something else

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A graduate of real promise is dismissed as not professional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'True potential' sounds like praise; 'potential' is the scramble instruction on TRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective for adjective: amateur work is done without professional skill, as in 'an amateur job'.

clue.text: Pieces broken by French spies found around motorway

parts.note: M = motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: French spies smash things up near a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken by French spies' reads as the spies doing the breaking; 'broken' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: fragments are the small bits left when something breaks.

clue.text: Relative force led to dam collapse

indicators.note: a collapsed dam falls apart, so its letters rearrange

parts.note: g is the symbol for the force of gravity
to lead a business is to run it: ran

explanation.surface: A comparative force caused a dam to give way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relative force' reads as physics; 'Relative' is the definition, a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the definition is a category, family member, and the answer one instance of it.

clue.text: Leading truck has problems with wipers

indicators.note: the leading letter of 'truck' is the one in front, its first

explanation.surface: The front lorry's windscreen wipers have gone wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wipers' calls up windscreen wipers, fitting the truck; here it means things you wipe with.
explanation.definitionFit: A playful coinage by function: tissues are what you wipe a nose or a spill with, so they are wipers.

clue.text: Rock fall by lake during exercise

indicators.note: what happens during something falls within it

parts.note: the tide falls when it ebbs

explanation.surface: A rockfall beside a lake interrupts a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock fall' reads as one event; split it, and 'Rock' alone is the definition while 'fall' is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A general word for a specific one: a pebble is a small, smooth rock.

clue.text: Low point of man beset with confusion

indicators.note: letters met with confusion are jumbled together

explanation.surface: Someone at their lowest ebb, overwhelmed by bewilderment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low point' reads as an emotional low; it is the lowest floor of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A literal reading of an idiom: the phrase usually means a bad moment, but the lowest point of a house is its basement.

clue.text: Bill's only change

parts.note: a bill is a poster, an advertisement: AD

explanation.surface: Bill's the only one who'll give you money back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name or an invoice; it is a bill posted on a wall, an ad.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb for verb: to adjust a setting is to change it a little.

clue.text: German agreement to censure another nation

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: Germany agrees to condemn a foreign country.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as diplomacy; 'German agreement' is simply the German word for yes.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: 'another' means a nation other than the Germany just mentioned, and the answer is one such.

clue.text: Celebrated socialist took in English politician

indicators.note: to take someone in is to let them inside

parts.note: a Member of Parliament is a politician

explanation.surface: A well-known left-winger welcomed a British MP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Celebrated' looks like the adjective famous describing the socialist; it is the verb, as in commemorated.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb for verb, past tense: an anniversary is celebrated when a person or event is honoured in memory.

clue.text: Weak-sounding stream

indicators.note: the word for weak is heard, not spelt

parts.note: poor = weak, as in a poor effort

explanation.surface: A feeble trickle of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weak-sounding stream' looks like a description of a trickle; 'stream' is a verb, to flow.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb for verb: rain or a crowd that streams out in a steady flow is said to pour.

clue.text: Just hit on ending to fox journalist

parts.note: a fox's tail is called its brush

explanation.surface: A reporter bumped into a plan to trick a fox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ending to fox' tempts you to take the last letter, X; it is the fox's tail, which is called a brush.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: to brush against something is to touch it lightly, only just making contact.

clue.text: Serious attention given to refuge

parts.note: to give someone your ear is to give them attention
a nest is a safe retreat

explanation.surface: Solemn care is given to providing a sanctuary.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs attention with refuge like a charity appeal; nothing in it hints at a person's manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective for adjective: an earnest person is serious and sincere in intent.
